Luxor: West Texas Power Prices Drove Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Down 9.13%

Bitcoin mining difficulty fell 9.13% on November 14, its largest decline since June. According to Luxor’s Hashrate Index, the drop was driven primarily by surging electricity prices in West Texas rather than falling BTC prices. A sharp decline in wind generation and transmission constraints pushed daily average power prices to $64–$122/MWh from November 7 to 11, above the roughly $54/MWh average breakeven level for miners operating at 25 J/TH. BTC Falls Below $60,000, ETH Drops Below $1,700 as 24H Liquidations Reach $1.57B

Coinbase: Only the US Dollar Gained Over the Past Month, While Crypto Performed Worst

According to Coinbase Institutional's November 20 weekly report, the US dollar was the only gainer among 14 tracked assets and market benchmarks over the 30 days through November 18, rising 2.5%. Bitcoin and Ethereum recorded the largest losses, falling 24.0% and 26.5%, respectively. Gold declined 10.2%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, and the S&P 500 dropped 4.3%. Coinbase attributed Bitcoin's weakness primarily to rising real yields and expectations of further Fed rate hikes. — link

Hardware wallet maker Ledger has updated its investigation into a supply chain tampering incident, confirming physically modified devices in Berlin, Germany. Two suspected devices in Dubai remain under investigation, while one affected Ledger Nano Gen 5 was identified in Southeast Asia.

Binance Hacker Moves $594M in ETH Over Two Days, Launders Funds via Chainflip and THORChain

According to Onchain Lens, the Binance hacker transferred approximately $594 million worth of ETH over the past two days, including $248 million on November 19 and another 197,460 ETH (approximately $346 million) on November 20. The funds were redistributed to new wallets, with some moved and swapped through cross-chain protocols including Chainflip and THORChain. Tracked hacker-linked wallets still hold approximately 226,665 ETH, worth around $395.6 million. — link
